@Sean Welleck, @Jeremy Avigad , Prasad Tetali, and I have submitted a paper to arXiv presenting ImProver - An agent-based proof optimization framework.

We introduce the problem of automated proof optimization as a generalization of neural theorem proving, in which we take an input theorem/proof and an arbitrary, user-defined metric, and aim to generate a new proof of the input theorem such that the new proof is both correct and maximizes this metric.

As an initial method and baseline for proof optimization, we find that naively applying LLMs to proof optimization falls short, and we incorporate various improvements into ImProver, such as the use of symbolic Lean context in a novel Chain-of-States technique, as well as error-correction and retrieval. We test ImProver on rewriting real-world undergraduate (MIL), competition (Compfiles), and research-level (Mathlib) mathematics theorems, finding that ImProver is capable of rewriting proofs so that they are substantially shorter, more modular, and more readable compared to the LLM baseline over all datasets.
